lastCompletedStory.title: Add fail-closed container toolchain assert to the preflight layer

openQuestions: While bringing `bun test` green for this story I hit a real, reproducible (not story-caused) flake: across ~30 full-suite `bun test` runs BEFORE any fix, 30-50% failed with 'this test timed out after 5000ms', always in a real-subprocess integration test (test/integration/journal-append-on-main.test.ts, test/integration/issue-file-on-main.test.ts, test/integration/ship-finalize-dirty-prd.test.ts Case A/B pairs, test/commands/setup-merge-mode.test.ts AC-7's test.each, test/interactivity/interactivity.test.ts's Esc-keypress test), never the same one twice, and never in my own new toolchain-assert.ts/test (a pure function with zero I/O). Root cause: bun's default 5000ms per-test timeout is too tight for real `git`/`claude`-on-PATH subprocess calls under this sandboxed environment's transient CPU contention (confirmed empirically that bunfig.toml's [test].timeout AND a preload setDefaultTimeout() workaround are BOTH silently ignored on this bun 1.2.23 -- ruled out as a fix path). Fix applied: added an explicit `{ timeout: 20_000 }` third argument to each of the affected tests (6 test blocks across 5 files) -- this brought 15/15 subsequent full-suite runs to 0 fail, and `bun run check:all` (the full spine) is green twice in a row. This is the SAME flake class already documented for CAM-186/CAM-201 (ink/terminal-size subprocess stalls) just manifesting via git/claude subprocess calls instead of ink renders -- see the new patterns.md bullet. Flagging per CAM-202 no-flaky-evasion discipline: if a DIFFERENT real-subprocess integration test (one of the other ~75 files using mkdtempSync + real git that I did NOT touch) starts timing out in a future story, apply the same `{ timeout: 20_000 }` fix rather than re-litigating root cause; this was not an exhaustive audit of every real-subprocess test in the repo, only the ones this session actually observed failing.

Also confirmed (unrelated aside, not actioned): the host sandbox's own `bun --version` is 1.2.23 while the repo's pinned `.bun-version` is 1.3.13 -- a live instance of exactly the drift class US-006/US-007 target, just on the HOST toolchain rather than the cam-worker CONTAINER toolchain. Out of scope for this story (which is container-only per its AC), but worth noting since it's the same failure mode this thread of stories is designed to catch.
nextStoryContext: US-007 (Auto-rebuild worker image on toolchain mismatch; escalate on rebuild failure) is next by priority. It wires assertContainerToolchain (src/supervisor/toolchain-assert.ts, this story) into the actual dispatch/ensure path: (1) preflightWorkerContainer (preflight-container.ts) needs a new branch that calls assertContainerToolchain and returns { ready:false, reason:'toolchain-mismatch' } (the reason string already exists in the type union from this story, just unwired to a real computation) -- likely needs a containerName + execFn added to PreflightWorkerContainerOptions, or a separate composing function that layers the toolchain check on top of the existing daemon/image checks; (2) ensureWorkerContainer (ensure-container.ts) needs a new branch (mirroring the existing 'image-stale' -> rm+rebuild branch) that reacts to 'toolchain-mismatch' by forcing a rebuild (docker rm -f + runWorkerContainer, action:'rebuilt') rather than reusing the running container; (3) per the story title, a rebuild FAILURE must escalate (fail-closed, no worker dispatch) -- follow the FirewallError/ContainerConfigError typed-throw convention (a new ToolchainMismatchError or reuse a rebuild-failure signal) so runSidecar's boot path can catch it and abort before entering runSidecarLoop, same as the firewall/config-repair steps do today. The exec seam for the actual bun/node probe inside the running container needs a production ToolchainExecFn wired the same way makeProductionEnsureContainerFn wires spawnFn/probe/statFn/firewallSpawnFn/configSpawnFn today (all spawnSync-backed, CI has no real docker so tests must inject fakes throughout, matching the DockerProbe/ConfigSpawnFn precedent).

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed via WebSearch + a live empirical test in a throwaway tmp fixture: `bun --version` prints the bare semver with no 'v' prefix (matches assertContainerToolchain's exact-match comparison for bun), `node --version` always prefixes 'v' (matches the stripLeadingV() comparison for node). Separately confirmed bunfig.toml's `[test].timeout` key (and a preload-script setDefaultTimeout() workaround) is silently ignored on this exact bun version -- ruled it out as a fix path for the flaky-timeout gate issue documented in openQuestions/patterns.md, used per-test `{ timeout: 20_000 }` overrides instead.
